- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns positive after a dip, model often lags; forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, model tends to overpredict; if below, underpredict; adjust toward moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum; add 1–2% buffer for final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.2 → -0.3 → +0.2), model overfits to recent noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average.
